summary: Autonomous vision analysis identified a irregular_patch of 2.04 ha (+/- 0.40 ha) at coordinates 15.7894 N, 74.2553 E between 2026-10-10 and 2026-10-25. Investigation mode: live_web_research. Public records research linked the event to Compensatory Ecological Afforestation / Corridor Protection. Investigation status: concluded_with_evidence.
detailed_findings: OpenCV 5 classical computer vision detected a significant forest recovery candidate covering 201 raster pixels (2.04 ha). The candidate region exhibited a major-to-minor aspect ratio of 2.28 and a compactness of 0.394. Investigation of public registries retrieved 6 records (Execution: live_web_research). Estimated tree impact ranges from None to None trees, based on None available.

citations.snippet:
Title: Study shows presence of 10 tigers and 46 leopards in Western Ghats | Goa News - The Times of India
* Study shows presence of 10 tigers and 46 leopards in Western Ghats. Keri: A study conducted by the Wildlife Conservation Trust (WCT), in association with the Sahyadri Tiger Reserve and the forest of territorial circle of Kolhapur, has shown the presence of eight adult tigers, two cubs, 46 leopards and nine dhole packs in the Western Ghats. The corridor between the Sahyadri Tiger Reserve and newly declared Conservation Reserves of Maharashtra to the Kali Tiger Reserve of Karnataka, shares borders with the Mhadei, Mahavir, Netravali and Cotigao Wildlife Sanctuaries and the Mollem National Park of Goa, and the Bhimgad Wildlife Sanctuary. The study also assessed the first ever density estimates for tigers and leopards in the Conservation Reserves of Maharashtra and the relative abundance indices for wild prey species of gaur and sambar. The study has identified bottlenecks, crossing points and gaps for wild mammals along with the state and national highways passing through the conservation reserves and adjoining forests. It has also set a baseline, which is vital to assess the impact of management actions or landscape change. “The corridor from the Sahyadri Tiger Reserve to the Kali Tiger Reserve is the only corridor that can allow movement of wildlife, including tigers to cross the landscape and plays key role in repopulating tigers in the Sahyadri Tiger Reserve,” said R M Ramanujan, principal conservation of forests (territory), Kolhapur, in the report. WCT president Anish Andhera said, “Protecting and monitoring the tiger corridor between Sahyadri and Kali Tiger Reserves are pivotal in improving the status of the tigers and other large mammals in this vast, multiple use landscape.”. With nearly 10 tigers in the Maharashtra corridor, and the connected tiger population of the Kali Tiger Reserve and the protected areas in Goa, we should see gradual colonisation by tigers up to the Sahyadri Tiger Reserve, which is located further north.”.
